briefs.headline: Liverpool and Chelsea draw 1-1 at Anfield; Liverpool go through 6-5 on penalties
briefs.summary: The Carabao Cup fourth-round meeting of two followed clubs finished level after two first-half penalties four minutes apart: Morgan Rogers converted for Chelsea in the 40th minute after Gravenberch fouled Caicedo, and Cody Gakpo converted for Liverpool in the 43rd after a Fofana handball. Liverpool won the shootout 6-5 after 16 kicks, Mamardashvili saving from Emegha and Joe Gomez scoring his first goal of any kind in 281 appearances before Fofana put the last kick over. Mike Penders started in goal for Chelsea and saved from Araujo and Barcola; Cole Palmer served his suspension; Florian Wirtz came off the bench in the 59th minute and scored his shootout kick; Lacroix went off injured at halftime. Attendance was 60,214. Liverpool host Bournemouth in the quarterfinals in the week of Dec. 14; Chelsea are out. Alonso called it 'a small setback, probably the least important competition for us,' and Iraola said 'luckily for us, we finished on the right side of the penalty shootout.'

briefs.headline: Wembanyama's 36 and 14 carry the Spurs past the Jazz in overtime for a third straight win
briefs.summary: Victor Wembanyama had 36 points, 14 rebounds, five assists, two blocks and two steals with no turnovers in 39 minutes, and San Antonio beat Utah one hundred seventeen to one hundred eleven in overtime at the Delta Center on Wednesday night. Utah led by as many as 11 and forced the extra period when Brice Sensabaugh and Keyonte George scored back-to-back baskets from five down; Sensabaugh opened overtime with a three before a 12 to nothing Spurs run settled it, Utah going two of seven with four turnovers in the period. Devin Vassell scored 21, 17 of them after halftime, and Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper had eight assists each. George scored a season-high 31 for the Jazz, who were without Jaren Jackson Jr., Lauri Markkanen and Jusuf Nurkic. The Spurs have three wins and two losses, are unbeaten in two road games, and host Minnesota on Saturday at 8 p.m. ET before Utah visits Monday.

briefs.headline: Crew beat FC Dallas 2-0 for a sixth win in seven league matches
briefs.summary: Gonzalo Tapia scored in the 18th minute from an Anass Zaroury cross and Santiago Rodriguez added the second in the 70th as the Crew beat FC Dallas at Toyota Stadium on Wednesday night, Patrick Schulte keeping the clean sheet behind a three-man back line. Columbus have 41 points from 32 matches and moved up to ninth in the Eastern Conference, the second of the two wild-card places, with D.C. United at home Saturday at 2 p.m. ET and Decision Day at Chicago on Nov. 7. Dallas stay second in the West on 54.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati draw 2-2 at Inter Miami after leading in the 86th minute
briefs.summary: Luis Suarez put Miami ahead in the 61st minute at Nu Stadium on Wednesday, Kenji Mboma Dem equalized in the 80th from an Evander pass, and Samuel Gidi's first MLS goal on the break in the 86th put Cincinnati in front before Riquelme Fillipi, also scoring his first MLS goal, leveled in the 90th from a Rodrigo De Paul assist. Ian Fray blocked Evander's chance in stoppage time. Cincinnati have 43 points from 32 matches and sit eighth in the East, level with seventh-place Orlando; ESPN's recap says they are still aiming to clinch a playoff place. Philadelphia visit TQL Stadium on Saturday at 2 p.m. ET, and MLS said Wednesday that the 2027 sprint season opens Feb. 19 with Miami hosting Cincinnati.

briefs.headline: Gibson will not name a Marshall starting quarterback for Old Dominion and says three could play
briefs.summary: Tony Gibson declined to name his starter for Saturday's 1 p.m. ET game at Old Dominion but indicated Zion Turner, Khalil Wilkins and Carlos Del Rio-Wilson could all play, with Del Rio-Wilson in line to return after Turner and Wilkins took the snaps against South Alabama, WV MetroNews reported Wednesday. Marshall are fourth in the Sun Belt East; Old Dominion are last in the division.

briefs.headline: Brewers beat the Rays 4-1 to win the World Series, the first title in the franchise's 57 years
briefs.summary: Milwaukee closed out the Series four games to one at Tropicana Field on Wednesday night behind Jacob Misiorowski, who threw five and two-thirds scoreless innings on two hits before leaving with a right calf cramp, and Trevor Megill, who finished with two innings. Rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt drove in two runs, singling home Brice Turang in the second and adding a sacrifice fly in the sixth after William Contreras' RBI double; Tampa Bay's only run came on Chandler Simpson's ninth-inning double off Megill. Contreras, who hit .381 in the Series and threw out four base stealers, was named MVP, the eighth catcher to win it. The Brewers won 103 regular-season games and went 11-2 in October.
briefs.source: MLB Stats API box score; ESPN

briefs.headline: 49ers reacquire DeForest Buckner from the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round pick
briefs.summary: San Francisco, at six wins and one loss, sent Indianapolis a 2027 fourth-rounder on Tuesday to bring back the defensive tackle it drafted seventh overall in 2016 and traded away in March 2020; Buckner had aired his frustration in Indianapolis on Oct. 18. ESPN frames it as the first move before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, with receiver help still a need. Thursday night's game is Carolina at Green Bay, 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video.

briefs.headline: Curry scores 44 as the Warriors hold off the Timberwolves; Rockets stay unbeaten
briefs.summary: Stephen Curry had 44 points, eight rebounds and six assists and Golden State beat Minnesota one hundred nineteen to one hundred fourteen on Wednesday; Jonathan Kuminga scored 20 for the Wolves. Houston routed Milwaukee by 32 to go to five wins and no losses, Fred VanVleet scoring 24, while Oklahoma City lost its first game, by 24 at Dallas, where Cooper Flagg had 26 points and eight assists. Nikola Jokic recorded his 200th career triple-double, 21 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists, in Denver's 13-point win over New Orleans.

briefs.headline: Big 12 fines UCF $100,000 over chants aimed at BYU and sets in-game penalties for a repeat
briefs.summary: The fine follows fans' chants at Saturday's overtime win over BYU that targeted the Mormon church. The league set a conference-wide policy Wednesday: an automatic minimum $100,000 fine and a warning on a first confirmed incident, a 15-yard unsportsmanlike penalty in football or a two-shot technical in basketball on a second incident in the same game, a possible $500,000 fine, and season-long bans for ejected fans. UCF said it is reviewing its options. Elsewhere, Sam Houston fired Phil Longo after a one-and-seven start, and the first College Football Playoff rankings come Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Carabao Cup quarterfinal draw sends Bournemouth to Anfield and Bradford to the Etihad
briefs.summary: Wednesday's other fourth-round results: Manchester City drew level with Brighton at two apiece and went through on penalties, Bournemouth beat Aston Villa by three goals to nil, Crystal Palace beat Fulham by a single Eddie Nketiah goal, and Sunderland beat Brentford by three goals to two. The draw for the week of Dec. 14 pairs Liverpool with Bournemouth, Crystal Palace with Sunderland, Manchester City with fourth-tier Bradford City and Fleetwood Town, who beat Arsenal on Tuesday, with the winner of Thursday's Everton-Newcastle tie. In Germany, Bayern Munich said Vincent Kompany left hospital Wednesday after Friday's collapse, diagnosed with meningeal irritation; assistant Aaron Danks led a six-goal cup win over Magdeburg.

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu wins 20 of 29 practice bouts in a knee supporter as the Kyushu basho nears, 10 days out
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu, who sat out the entire September tournament after July surgery on his right knee, went on degeiko (visiting practice) at Sakaigawa stable in Onojo, Fukuoka, on Thursday and took 29 straight bouts against top-division wrestler Hiradoumi, winning 20 after starting with two wins in his first five, Sankei Shimbun reported. He said his tachiai (initial charge) is 'coming back little by little' and he is training intending to compete in the Kyushu basho (tournament), which opens Sunday, Nov. 8, at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center and runs through Nov. 22; a final decision rests with his stablemaster. Fellow yokozuna Onosato held his first Fukuoka practice Tuesday, basics only, chasing a seventh yusho (championship) and his first back-to-back titles. The Japan Sumo Association's site lists the tournament sold out.

sections.label: On the Water
sections.note: Readings are from out/fishing.json, fetched at 5:40 a.m. ET Thursday, and the USGS and NOAA records behind it; the fetcher's 24-hour comparison fields again sit about 48 hours back. The Fisherman's Post Topsail/Sneads Ferry report is monthly: the newest is the October report, published Oct. 1 and 27.9 days old this morning, past this paper's 21-day gate, so what's running below is the reference calendar's seasonal pattern, labeled as such, not a live report. No 2026 fall trout delivery to the Williams, the Cranberry or the Summersville tailwater is confirmed by any outlet.

waters.reading: 85.4 cfs, 1.55 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on discharge and on stage against 103.0 cfs and 1.65 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Down 8.4 cfs and 0.05 feet on the day against the USGS trace's 93.8 cfs and 1.60 feet at 5:15 a.m. Wednesday, Wednesday's edition reading, a 12th straight falling morning with the recession still slowing (20, 16, 9, 9, 8), and the trace shows a clean stair-step with no rain bump: 93.8 at 6 a.m. Wednesday, 90.4 by noon, 88.7 at 6 p.m., 87.0 at midnight, 85.4 from about 5 a.m. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, printed as it stands, "85 cfs - prime wading water.", and the fetcher's 103.0 cfs and 1.65 feet comparison points match the trace's 5:15 a.m. Tuesday values, about 48 hours old, so the 18-cfs drop they imply is two days' worth; the falling flags are right in direction. At 85 and clear after twelve days of recession the pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the file records as its structure are wadeable across at this flow and the fish are where the water still moves: the heads and seams of the plunge pools and the shade of the undercuts, not the flat tailouts. Low, clear water in late October is a long-leader, small-fly problem: a 12-foot leader to 6X, a size 18 to 20 blue-winged olive or a small parachute Adams on top in the afternoon, a size 18 pheasant tail or zebra midge dropped 18 inches under it through the morning, and a small olive or black woolly bugger swung through the deeper pools at dusk. Drab clothing and an upstream approach count for more than the pattern at this clarity.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.68 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 24.62 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.7 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the pool steady, up 0.06 against its 24.62 comparison point; against the USGS trace's 24.86 at 5 a.m. Wednesday, Wednesday's edition reading, the gauge is down 0.18 on the day, inside the fetcher's 0.25-foot band, so steady holds on the day though the day's direction is down where the comparison implies up. The trace shows the pool easing through Wednesday, 24.91 at midnight, 24.82 at 6 a.m., 24.65 at noon, 24.57 at 9 p.m. and a 24.54 evening low, then edging back up a tenth overnight to 24.68 at 5 a.m.; the Williams above showed no rain. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 24.7 the gauge is 2.3 feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27 feet. At normal pool the river fishes the structure and what current it makes: shad are the forage and skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam and along the riprap where the eddy line forms, and a crawfish-colored jig or a three-inch tube dragged on the rock for the smallmouth and drum holding tight. A pool that slipped a quarter foot and steadied leaves the fish on the same edges as Wednesday.

Steady low water below the dam keeps the fish on the current edges the structure makes: the forage is shad and skipjack with crawfish in the riprap, so a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of each wing dam rather than the eddy behind it, a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head along the lock wall's seam for the sauger starting to stack as the water cools, and cut skipjack on the bottom below the dam's discharge for blue and flathead catfish after dark.

waters.working: Waning gibbous, three days past full: the fetcher's file carries the moon at 88 percent lit and 18.0 days old, and the spring tides are starting to come off the water, the sound's morning high holding at 4.7 feet but the evening high down to 3.4 and the surf high to 6.1. The sound at Hampstead bottomed at 0.1 feet at 5:12 a.m. and is on its flood at press time, filling 4.6 feet to the 4.7-foot high at 11:27 a.m.; it drains 4.2 feet to a 0.5-foot low at 6:16 p.m., fills 2.9 feet to a 3.4-foot high at 11:48 p.m. and drains toward Friday's early low, which falls outside today's table. All four sound events land inside today; nothing carries a spillover tag. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: low 3:33 a.m. at -0.1, high 10:16 a.m. at 6.1, low 4:46 p.m. at 0.2, high 10:36 p.m. at 4.1, so the sound lags the surf by 71 and 72 minutes on the highs and 99 and 90 minutes on the lows this morning, the long-lag-on-the-ebb pattern the reference describes. Beaufort's thermometer, 60 miles up the coast, read 66.2F at 5:30 a.m., up 1.4 on the day. What's running is the reference calendar's seasonal pattern, not a live report: the Fisherman's Post October report is 27.9 days old and past the 21-day gate, and no November report has posted on either the Fisherman's Post or the Coastal Angler feed. October's pattern is the spot run at its peak with red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, and November's, three days off, puts speckled trout at prime. Tide is the whole game here: the afternoon ebb, 11:27 a.m. to 6:16 p.m., is the day's long window, and red drum want the last of it, so cut menhaden or a quarter-ounce jighead with a Gulp shrimp fan-cast a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges as the grass drains from about 3:30 p.m.; speckled trout on the first of the evening flood behind the 6:16 p.m. low, a popping cork with live shrimp over the oyster edges or a soft plastic worked slow as the light goes; spot and black drum on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the channel on either side of the 11:27 a.m. high; sheepshead with fiddlers tight to the bridge pilings on the moving water. NWS Wilmington, read at 5:48 a.m.: a High Rip Current Risk for Coastal Pender through 8 p.m. today with a strong north-to-south longshore current, new since Wednesday; a Coastal Flood Advisory from 9 a.m. to noon, up to half a foot of inundation along the Intracoastal Waterway and tidal creeks; and a Small Craft Advisory on the coastal waters out 20 nautical miles until midnight tonight, seas 4 to 6 feet. The surf is not a fishing proposition today.
